chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
It is disliked to combine the two Surahs in the obligatory prayer, but as for the optional prayer, there is no problem.

key_terms.السُّورَتَيْنِ: the two Surahs (chapters of the Quran)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to combine two Surahs in one rak'ah of prayer?
ai.summary: Reported through the chain of Zurarah from Imam al-Baqir, this hadith clarifies the juristic preference against merging two Surahs in obligatory prayers to maintain ritual distinctness, while permitting flexibility in voluntary prayers. This distinction reflects the Shia emphasis on preserving the structural integrity of the Fard prayer while allowing ease in Nafl, a principle often discussed in Usul al-Fiqh regarding the conditions of valid recitation.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘But rather, it is disliked that one should gather between the two Chapters during the Obligatory (Salāt). But, as for the Optional (Salāt), so there is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is undesirable to recite two Surah (chapters) together in an obligatory Salah (prayer) but in an optional one it is not harmful.’” (Ahadith 7-11 are best explained in the form of fatwa.)
